names.iupac: Propanamide, N-phenyl-N-[1-(2-phenylethyl)-4-piperidinyl]- (CAS index name, as listed by NIST); EUDA prints 'N-(1-(2-phenethyl)-4-piperidinyl-N-phenyl-propanamide'

forms.detail: EUDA: fentanyl and its salts are white granular or crystalline powders; DEA Diversion: fentanyl is a solid that exists as a crystal or crystalline powder.

EUDA: fentanyl citrate solutions for injection, transdermal patches, transmucosal lozenges and buccal tablets (Effentora). DEA Diversion (United States): oral transmucosal lozenges (Actiq), effervescent buccal tablets (Fentora), sublingual tablets (Abstral), sublingual sprays (Subsys), nasal sprays (Lazanda), transdermal patches (Duragesic and generics), injectable formulations (Sublimaze, historically).
DEA: counterfeit pills made to imitate pharmaceutical drugs; DEA Diversion: fake prescription pills.
DEA: fentanyl spiked onto blotter paper; EUDA: 'paper trips', thin cardboard impregnated with fentanyl.

EUDA names alfentanil, sufentanil, remifentanil, carfentanil, 3-methylfentanyl (cis and trans forms), alpha-methylfentanyl, acetyl-alpha-methylfentanyl, alpha-methylthiofentanyl, beta-hydroxyfentanyl, beta-hydroxy-3-methylfentanyl, 3-methylthiofentanyl, para-fluorofentanyl and thiofentanyl (spellings standardized; EUDA hyphenates some differently); the WHO ATC index lists alfentanil, sufentanil and remifentanil as opioid anaesthetics. EUDA mentions an illicit light yellow powder called 'White Persian' that contained 3-methylfentanyl.
